intro.title: Grid vs Flex: when to use which
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage layout to understand when to use CSS Grid versus CSS Flexbox. You'll learn the core concept of choosing the right layout model based on whether you need one-dimensional (Flexbox) or two-dimensional (Grid) control. The main technologies involved are CSS Grid for overall page structure and CSS Flexbox for aligning items within sections. By the end, you'll be able to decide which tool to use for common layout tasks, applying your knowledge through hands-on coding exercises.
intro.usecase: Understanding when to use CSS Grid versus Flexbox is essential for building modern, responsive layouts in real-world applications. For example, a product dashboard uses Grid to create a two-dimensional layout of cards, charts, and widgets arranged in rows and columns, while a navigation menu or a filter bar relies on Flexbox for one-dimensional alignment of items horizontally or vertically. Developers choose Grid for overall page structure, like a news article with a sidebar and main content, and Flexbox for components within those sections, such as a button group or a list of tags. Mastering this distinction allows you to efficiently build complex interfaces like admin panels, e-commerce product grids, or interactive data tables that adapt seamlessly across devices.
